Whether 'n1-' funders (n1-payments, n1-payments-2, n1-multichain) belong to Near One: no source fetched states it (a search for the accounts returned nothing).
Whether Near-One/transaction-bench (repo not publicly reachable, only a Docker image) is what runs tx-bench.near and whether it issues sign calls.
Whether any signature produced is broadcast on another chain (not checkable by us).
Who waclaw.near is (account funded the creator in 2024; no identity source found).
Real total volume of tx-bench sign calls: our sample is stratified (~2,000 sign receipts per month), so per-month counts are not volumes. The ~1.2M estimate is the caller's, not re-derived here.

benchmark_analysis.summary: Strong behavioural signature of a scheduled synthetic/monitoring load (probably a liveness/latency probe or benchmark): fixed cadence, alternating ECDSA/EdDSA, random never-reused payloads, no path, all success, 24/7, one key. Explicit proof of purpose (docs/repo naming it) was NOT found, so the label stays 'unknown - suspected benchmark'.
benchmark_analysis.sample_scope: 15,492 sign receipts of tx-bench.near in sample_parsed.csv.gz (of 177,727 rows total; sample is cluster windows of 200 consecutive v1.signer txs per census/sample, ~2,000 sign receipts/month).

months_active_in_sample.reading: Not flat in share: ramps up 2025-04 to a peak in 2025-08/09 (it dominates ~95% of sign requests that month), then declines steadily to ~4-5% by late 2026. Whether this is the account lowering its cadence or others growing is not separable from the sample; per-minute cadence inside a window is constant (see timing).

benchmark_analysis.requests_per_cluster: Up to 100 per 200-tx cluster (e.g. 2025-09-c10: 100 of 100 sign receipts are tx-bench); cluster-level share of sign receipts: min 0, median 12.9%, max 100% (all clusters, all accounts).

key_type_mix.by_month: 2025-04..2025-10: 100% legacy; 2025-11: 666 legacy / 269 ECDSA / 266 EdDSA (switch month); 2025-12 onward: 100% payload_v2 with ECDSA:EdDSA ~1:1 every month (e.g. 2026-03: 295/294, 2026-09: 101/105).

payload_repetition.constant_payloads: Only in legacy period: 0101..01 (32x byte 0x01) in all 154 receipts of 2025-04 and 0505..05 (32x 0x05) in all 140 of 2025-05 - these are placeholder-looking values, not real hashes.
payload_repetition.random_payloads: All other 15,198 receipts: 14,878 distinct; first-hex-digit histogram flat (907-1021 per digit), i.e. looks uniformly random 32 bytes. No payload repeats across different txs (apart from the two constants); apparent duplicates are the same tx_hash seen in two overlapping clusters.
payload_repetition.caveat: Random-looking payloads are consistent with both random test data and real tx sighash values; we cannot tell them apart without seeing the chain.

tx_shape.signer: tx-bench.near itself (15,492/15,492), single public key ed25519:9XMdCm...1HYbrYEn (= creation key)
tx_shape.actions: exactly one FunctionCall (v1.signer.sign) per tx; no batching, no other actions
tx_shape.args: legacy: {key_version, path, payload[32 ints]}; new: {domain_id, path, payload_v2}

timing.cadence: Inside a window, consecutive tx-bench txs are separated by a median 59.7 s (25th-75th pct 50.8-60.2 s); in 2025-09-c10 the 99 gaps are 98-103 blocks (~100 blocks, ~99 min total for 100 txs, one tx every ~60 s). From 2025-11 on, requests come as an ECDSA+EdDSA pair every ~60 s (gaps alternate 7-10 s / 49-54 s, e.g. 2026-03-c05: 7,54,7,53,7,52...). Block-height gap mode 96-101 (legacy, one request/minute) and 12-13 (the intra-pair gap at ~1 s/block plus nearby).
timing.breaks: 90th-99th percentile gaps ~898-902 s = 15 min: occasional pauses of a round 15 min, i.e. clockwork rather than organic traffic.
timing.volume_profile: Hour-of-day (UTC) of 15,492 txs: every hour 414-906 (no day/night pattern) => 24/7 machine activity.
timing.interpretation: Inference (c): strongly machine-scheduled, e.g. cron/loop at 60 s.

benchmark_analysis.fulfilment: receipt_status Success 15,492; callback_status Success 15,492; fulfilled=1 15,492 => 0 failed in sample (the account is not stress-testing capacity: ~1 req/min is far below MPC throughput).
benchmark_analysis.cross_chain_use: Cannot be verified: sign output returns only a signature; we have no chain target, path is empty, payloads not mapped to tx hashes on any chain. Absence of evidence is weak. Inference: with empty path, derived key = the account's own root-derived key; no deposit beyond 1 yocto; random payloads and constant 0x01/0x05 payloads suggest probe traffic rather than real transfers.
supporting_inferences_for_suspected_benc: Name 'tx-bench' plus sibling 'tx-bench-buddy.near', both created in the same session by a throwaway implicit account.
Fixed ~60 s cadence, 24/7, with 15-min pauses; ECDSA+EdDSA alternation after domain-id upgrade (tests both schemes) - coverage-style behaviour.
Random or constant (0x01/0x05) payloads, empty path, 1 yocto deposit, 100% success, single-action txs.
Recurring large NEAR top-ups (100-300 NEAR) from 'n1-payments-2.near' show a funded, maintained operation, not a one-off test.
Near One publishes a 'transaction-bench' image measuring end-user transaction latency (name match; unconfirmed link).
missing_proof: Any document naming tx-bench.near as a Near One / NEAR Foundation tool (repo config, README, dashboard, docs, blog).
Confirmation that n1-* accounts are Near One.
Source of Near-One/transaction-bench (404) to see whether it calls v1.signer.sign and uses account name 'tx-bench.near'.
evidence_that_would_settle_it: Near One / MPC team statement or a public repo/config containing 'tx-bench.near' (ask Near One: github.com/Near-One/transaction-bench maintainers).
An identity link for waclaw.near or the n1-* accounts (e.g. their listing in a Near One document, or their appearing as Near One multisig/treasury).
Their dashboards for MPC latency (if tx-bench.near is a latency monitor, its sign txs will match published latency numbers).
benchmark_analysis.category_decision: category_suggestion = 'unknown' (suspected benchmark). 'benchmark-test' not justified: no explicit source names the account or its creator/funder as benchmark tooling. Recommended wording in THESIS: 'a single account with machine-scheduled, probe-like behaviour (1 request/min, random payloads), suspected benchmark/monitoring; not attributed'. Report its share separately so conclusions hold with and without it.
